DESIGN NOTES
SETUP GUIDE

Support the hub.
Free the shaft.

Illustrative 14 mm hub with a 10 mm through-bore length. Motor and hub are reference geometry, not printable parts.

Download complete kit ↓Editable OpenSCAD source
FROM SCREEN TO WORKBENCH
01 / CHECK

Measure before printing.

NEMA17 describes the motor frame, not a guaranteed shaft size. This set assumes a 5 mm shaft, an accessible shaft end, and an open-ended hub. Measure your hub and the space beneath it.

02 / PRINT

Start with a fit check.

Use PETG or nylon, 0.2 mm layers and 6+ walls. Start at 60% infill for supports; solid punches. Place punches flange-down. Print plates top-face-down for support-free underside seats. Print two risers.

03 / REMOVE

Keep the load off the bearings.

Remove set screws. Seat a plate beneath the hub, with the motor hanging freely between the risers. Press the shaft end gently downward. Catch the motor as it releases. Stop if a tool bends or slips.

Prototype geometry, not load-rated tooling. The printed punches are for light hand pressure and alignment. For tight interference fits, use a properly supported steel punch and metal support tooling. Do not hammer these parts. Blind sleeves cannot be removed with this through-punch setup. Installation needs direct rear shaft support; resting the motor casing on a platform loads its bearings.
